newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany, Dasa agree price for Eurofighter - sources.
newsitem.headline: Germany, Dasa agree price for Eurofighter - sources.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), contractor in the Eurofighter project, have agreed on price for Bonn to buy 180 of the combat jets, coalition sources said on Friday.

The sources confirmed a report in the Berliner Zeitung newspaper which said the two sides had reached a compromise price of "over 20 billion marks ($12.7 billion) " for the full production run -- down from Dasa's original asking price of 26 billion marks.

Ruehe, speaking on the Pro7 television channel, declined to confirm the price details -- which he said were subject to the approval of both government and parliament -- but said he was happy with the negotiations.
"The talks are going very well and the logistical problems can be solved," Ruehe told Pro7. Reports that Ruehe met Dasa Chief Executive Manfred Bischoff on Friday could not be confirmed.

News of progress will come as a relief to Eurofighter partners Britain, Italy and Spain, who are all keen to ensure that financing is put in place to ensure that serial production of the 21st century Eurofighter can begin as soon as possible.
Britain wants to buy 232 Eurofighters, Italy 140 and Spain 87. All have been unsettled by a tense waiting game in Bonn as the axe of budget austerity has hung over defence procurement.
British Aerospace, Alenia Spa of Italy and Spain's CASA are all partners with Dasa in the Eurofighter consortium.
Despite a crunch in the defence budget, Ruehe has won a pledge from Finance Minister Theo Waigel to release extra funds from the federal budget to help finance the Eurofighter.

Ruehe said he was optimistic Germany would take delivery of the full 180 Eurofighters he had originally wanted. "We need a fighter jet. We have negotiated well. And we have shown how important it was to save money," he said.
"But we must still reach a decision on how the whole project is to be financed over the next few years. It must be completely solid and serious," Ruehe added.
Delivery of 140 Eurofighters would begin in 2002, while a further 40 modified ground attack aircraft would come later.
In addition to the overall project price, Bonn has been haggling with Dasa -- aerospace unit of auto giant Daimler-Benz AG -- over startup payments for the Eurofighter.
"The decisions still have to be made and only then will we sign a contract," Ruehe said.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.577 German Marks)
